integrity of the mechanical seal support system

facts.title: audit finding - assurance activity of material unwanted event control at P-7112

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was no injury or loss. The potential outcome was rated 3 against the site's consequence scale, above the 0 actually realised.

defences.finding: Control HYDROCARBON_TRANSFER_CONTROL: the controlled transfer of hydrocarbon between vessels had been bypassed, and the learning team review classified this as an individual or team action.

Control SEAL_FACE_TEMPERATURE_ALARM: the seal-face high-temperature alarm and trip had degraded below its design intent, and the learning team review classified this as a task or environmental condition.

Control SEAL_SUPPORT_SYSTEM_INTEGRITY: the integrity of the mechanical seal support system was in place but did not perform, and the learning team review classified this as an absent or failed defence.

recommendations: Restore the integrity of the mechanical seal support system on P-7112 and record the assurance activity before this task is next authorised.
response.sequence: Work was under way in maintaining sealing systems on rotating equipment, specifically monitoring seal-face condition and temperature. P-7112 (export transfer pumps) is in service for tank-to-jetty product transfer, same seal class as the Marrindal family. The task proceeded during cleaning and preparation while the controlled transfer of hydrocarbon between vessels had been bypassed. The pressure energy involved is held as hydraulic accumulator, and the recorded presentation was jet release, stored-energy discharge, rupture.
response.summary: On 8 September 2025 a planned assurance activity of P-7112 at Cape Verity Export Terminal found the controlled transfer of hydrocarbon between vessels not effective.
